rateLimit.description: Per-key token bucket shared across protected routes, initially full, refilled using monotonic elapsed time. Invalid authenticated requests consume tokens. Rate-limit rejections do not consume a token. Public GET routes are unmetered even with credentials. Buckets reset on restart; replicas have independent allowances. These values describe this process configuration.

resources.description: The executable runs one calculation worker, with a bounded FIFO queue shared across keys. The calculation deadline includes queue wait and ends at the worker result, excluding JSON transfer. Admission follows authentication, rate limiting and validation. A full queue returns server_busy; recovery or shutdown returns not_ready; an expired calculation returns calculation_timeout with no partial result. Worker loss returns calculation_failed and rejects queued jobs as not_ready. Saturation alone does not fail readiness. Timed out active work terminates the worker before replacement. Deadlines are enforced by the HTTP event loop, subject to scheduling delay. The socket cap drops excess TCP connections without an HTTP response. Header timeout is the smaller of headersTimeoutMs and requestTimeoutMs; request timeout and socket inactivity timeout both use requestTimeoutMs. The shutdown deadline can end connections before their own deadlines.

configuration.logSink: child stdout pipe continuously drained and discarded
configuration.keyAssignment: one distinct key per concurrent connection; the same pool remains configured across all trials

methodology.transport: HTTP/1.1 loopback keep-alive; client and server are separate processes on this machine
methodology.load: closed loop, fixed connections, pipelining 1, no target arrival rate; uncorrected observed latency
methodology.latency: autocannon full-response events in ms, ceil to ns, Node HDR histogram with 3 significant digits; p50 and p95 queried directly
methodology.throughput: completed HTTP 200 responses divided by monotonic elapsed seconds from performance.now around the autocannon invocation through its completion callback, including client setup and aggregation
methodology.clocks: durationSeconds is monotonic; requestedDurationSeconds is the configured target; autocannonDurationSeconds is its wall-clock duration rounded to 0.01s; start/finish timestamps are wall clock
methodology.cutoff: autocannon destroys in-flight requests at the time limit; sent minus completed are excluded from latency
methodology.verification: every full body parsed and checked for engine identity, receipt scopes and minimal receipt shape; no independent accuracy claim
methodology.order: repetition, then workload order, then connection order; a separate warmup precedes each measurement
methodology.barriers: after each warmup and measurement, await an unmeasured calculation on the same FIFO to finish earlier-admitted jobs

limitations: Shared host; CPU model and visible limits do not establish exclusive resources or hidden ancestor limits.
Client JSON checks and log draining consume this machine too; no remote client, TLS, reverse proxy or container is measured.
One repeated synthetic input per route; no mix, varied dates, long soak, overload capacity or astronomical accuracy claim.
Buckets are raised for throughput measurement; production defaults impose lower per-key allowances.
Closed-loop results and unfinished tails do not represent latency under a fixed external arrival rate.
No general service-level objective or production sizing guarantee follows from these runs.
